descriptionChirho: To bow down or kneel as an act of worship, reverence, submission, or prayer before God or a superior (Qal stem).
To crouch or hunker down like an animal, especially of a lion crouching or an animal settling on its legs (Qal stem, distinct physical posture rather than worship).
To bow or buckle from weakness or feebleness, said of knees that totter or give way (Qal participle describing physical collapse rather than intentional kneeling).
To cause someone to bow down or fall, to bring low, subdue, or strike down an enemy or opponent (Hifil causative stem).
